newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican coffee crops unharmed by frost so far.
newsitem.headline: Mexican coffee crops unharmed by frost so far.

text.p: Mexico's coffee crop has not been significantly damaged by freezing cold temperatures that have afflicted the north of the country, coffee farmers told Reuters Tuesday.
"The bad weather until now has not affected us," said Ciro de la Bequia, a coffee farmer in the higher altitudes of Huatusco, Veracruz state.

Officials at the Mexican Coffee Exporters Association and Confederation of Mexican Coffee Growers said their members have not reported any damage in key coffee producing regions susceptible to winter frosts in Puebla and Veracruz states.

"There have been low temperatures because of the bad weather especially in the north of Puebla, but I don't think there has been any damage," confederation executive director Juan Carlos Villareal said.

La Jornada newspaper reported 2,000 hectacres of crops damaged in the minor coffee producing state of Hidalgo because of frost, but neither the association nor the confederation could confirm the report.

"There have not been frosts but harvesters have not gone out to pick the beans because of the cold," said Jenaro Hernandez de la Mora, a Veracruz state farmer and the association's executive director.

Leaving the beans on the trees a few extra days should not hurt the harvest as no frosts are expected to hit Mexico's coffee producing region through the weekend, said Mike Palmerino of the Weather Services Corporation.
The higher altitude regions of Puebla and Veracruz are the most likely to be affected by frosts.

Veracruz was last harvest's top producing state in the country, at about 1.42 million 60-kg bags, surpassing Chiapas, traditionally the nation's top producing state, which produced 1.31 million bags, according to the Mexican Coffee Council.
Puebla produced 795,743 bags in the 1995-1996 coffee season and Oaxaca harvested 675,042 bags, according to council figures.

Mexico's annual production of coffee is notoriously difficult to predict and estimate, although coffee exports believe it oscilates between about 3.9 million 60-kg bags and over five million 60 kg-bags.
